steps.intro: I read two months of your comments about decks and about 350 decks you answered. One question to pin down the goal before the details.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Is this the right job description for the decks?
steps.today: Decks ask you things and record your answers. Nothing written down says what they are for.
steps.problem: Each chat guesses. Some ask you to approve build details; others quietly decide things you wanted to decide.
steps.proposal: One rule for every deck: you decide how the app looks, behaves and how its parts fit together. I decide how to build it, and show you those calls so you can overrule them. Yes makes this the rule.

steps.intro: The two faults you named are already fixed in this deck, so you can check them as you go. Then two new ideas.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: The green circle behind "answered" is gone.
steps.changed: The circle was the big tick from the "submitted" screen leaking onto every answered question and stretching the card.
steps.notice: Press an answer here and look at the top of this card: a small green "answered" beside the question number, nothing else.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: A question you answer by typing now has one box, not two.
steps.changed: A typed-answer question used to show its own box and the usual note box side by side. The note box is now left off those questions.
steps.notice: The very last question in this deck is a typed one. It has a single box.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Should every question get three one-tap replies for when no option fits?
steps.today: Your only escapes are Other and Don't know. You used Other on 1 question in 5, and Don't know mostly to say the question itself was wrong.
steps.problem: I then have to guess from your note whether you mean "outdated", "explain more" or "just handle it".
steps.proposal: Add three buttons beside Something else: You decide, I need more context, That's not right. Each tells me exactly what to do next. Don't know goes away.

options.label: All three
pros: One tap instead of a typed explanation.
A wrong or outdated question gets fixed, not argued in a note.
cons: Four small buttons under every question instead of one or two.

options.label: Only "more context" and "not right"
pros: Fewer buttons.
cons: No quick way to hand a small choice back to me.

options.label: Leave it
pros: Nothing new to learn.
cons: I keep guessing what an Other note means.

steps.caption: A drawing of the proposal, not built yet.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Should you be able to click a spot on a picture and comment on exactly that spot?
steps.today: A picture step gives you Yes, No, Other and one note box for the whole picture.
steps.problem: You end up describing where things are: "the card at the top", "the button on the right". Some rounds repeated because I fixed the wrong part.
steps.proposal: Click anywhere on a picture to drop a numbered pin and type a comment for that spot. I get the exact place with each comment.

options.label: Add pins
pros: Steer one small element without describing where it is.
Several separate comments on one picture stay separate.
cons: One more thing on the page; the note box stays for general remarks.

options.label: Leave it
pros: Simpler page.
cons: You keep describing locations in words.

steps.caption: A drawing of the proposal, not built yet.

steps.page: What every deck must tell you
steps.intro: Your most repeated complaints: not enough context, too many words, and questions built on facts that were out of date.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Should every deck open with a short "before you start" page?
steps.today: A deck opens straight on its first question.
steps.problem: You have asked "what is this deck?" and "what am I approving?" more than once. Nothing says how long it is or what happens after.
steps.proposal: One opening page: what this is, how many decisions, roughly how long, what you will see, and what happens next.

options.label: Add the opening page
pros: You know what you are in for before question one.
cons: One extra click on every deck, even a two-question one.

options.label: Only on decks with 6 or more questions
pros: Short decks stay instant.
cons: A short deck can still be confusing.

options.label: Leave it
pros: No extra page.
cons: Decks keep opening cold.

steps.caption: A drawing of the proposal, not built yet.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Should each question have to show how its "Today" fact was checked?
steps.today: Whoever writes a deck states what exists today from memory or old notes. Nothing makes them check.
steps.problem: Your worst decks asked about work that was already finished, already in progress, or never true. You then had to work out what was real.
steps.proposal: A deck is refused unless each question says how its Today was checked that day. You see it as one small line under the question.

options.label: Check, and show the line
pros: You can see at a glance the fact is fresh.
A lazy check is visible to you.
cons: One more line of small text per question.

options.label: Check, but do not show it
pros: Cleaner page.
cons: You cannot tell a real check from a box-tick.

options.label: Leave it
pros: Decks are quicker to write.
cons: Out-of-date questions keep reaching you.

steps.caption: A drawing. The green "Checked today" line is the new part.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Should a question about how something looks be refused without a picture?
steps.today: Written questions had no way to show a picture until today. This deck is the first that can.
steps.problem: On the phone-layout deck you answered Other on 7 of 10 written questions, mostly "I need to see it".
steps.proposal: Every question is marked as about looks, behaviour, wording or priorities. One about looks will not build without a picture or drawing.

options.label: Refuse without a picture
pros: You never have to imagine a layout from a paragraph.
cons: Decks about looks take me longer to prepare.

options.label: Allow it, but warn the writer
pros: Faster decks.
cons: Some picture-less look questions will still reach you.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Should the builder cap how much text a question can carry?
steps.today: Headlines are capped at 25 words. The three explanation boxes are not; recent ones ran 60 to 150 words each.
steps.problem: You wrote "wall of text" and "way too much copy". Long boxes also hide two or three decisions inside one question.
steps.proposal: Each box is capped at 40 words and each question asks one thing. Longer is refused, so it must be split or cut.

options.label: Hard cap, refuse longer
pros: Every question reads in seconds.
Bundled questions get split apart.
cons: A complicated topic becomes more, smaller questions.

options.label: Warn only
pros: Room for the odd long explanation.
cons: Warnings get ignored; text creeps back.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Should decks list the small calls I made for you, instead of asking each one?
steps.today: Small choices are either asked as full questions or made silently.
steps.problem: Asked, they bury the real decisions ("just show me what you are unsure about"). Silent, you find surprises later.
steps.proposal: A "Calls I made for you" list at the end: one line each with my reason. Each is Fine unless you tap Change this.

options.label: Add the list
pros: Fewer questions, no silent decisions.
Overruling one is a single tap.
cons: You must skim the list, or small calls stand by default.

options.label: Ask everything as a question
pros: Nothing stands without your answer.
cons: Long decks; the big decisions get lost.

options.label: Leave it
pros: Shortest decks.
cons: Silent calls keep surprising you.

steps.caption: A drawing of the proposal, not built yet.

steps.intro: You said the contract decks do not help. Every one of the last 15 was signed in under 90 seconds, most in under 10 — nobody could read 26 rows that fast.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: What should replace the contract deck?
steps.today: Before building, you sign a table of one-line "done" statements. After, the same table returns with pass or fail beside each.
steps.problem: It does not show what exists, how the parts fit, or how it is tested. You called it "piss poor" at helping you understand the build.
steps.proposal: A walkthrough in the normal deck style: what it is for, every screen with its picture and the decision behind it, behind the scenes in plain steps, calls I made, how it is tested, what is left. Every item can be changed.

options.label: Walkthrough before and after building
pros: You steer the plan before work starts, then check the result against it.
Same shape both times, so the second is quick.
cons: Two long decks per big feature. The first uses drawings for unbuilt screens.

options.label: Walkthrough only after building
pros: One deck. Every picture is the finished screen.
cons: A misunderstanding is found after the work is done.

options.label: Keep the contract table
pros: Nothing to build.
cons: You keep signing something you do not read.
options.caption: The contract deck as it is today.

steps.caption: A drawing of two parts of a walkthrough: one screen, and one behind-the-scenes story.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: What should have to be true before a feature counts as finished?
steps.today: A check refuses to finish a feature until the contract is signed and a separate reviewer has graded every row.
steps.problem: You have told chats to skip the contract, the grader or both at least six times. The check guards a step you no longer want.
steps.proposal: Finished means: you submitted the walkthrough and nothing in it is still marked Change this.

options.label: Your walkthrough, nothing left to change
pros: One clear finish line that you control.
cons: No independent reviewer unless you ask for one.

options.label: Walkthrough plus a quiet independent check
pros: A second pair of eyes tests each promise; you only hear about failures.
cons: Slower and costs more per feature.

options.label: No check at all
pros: Fastest.
cons: A chat could call something finished that you never saw.

steps.intro: Last page: links that die, and too many separate decks.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Should decks run from one always-on service so links stop dying?
steps.today: Each deck is run by the chat that made it. When that chat ends or restarts, the link dies. It also shuts down the moment you submit.
steps.problem: You have written "deck died" or "relaunch deck" at least 19 times, and sometimes could not tell whether your answers went through.
steps.proposal: One small deck service that starts when you log in to this computer. Every deck keeps a permanent link and can be reopened after submitting. This adds a login service to your system.

options.label: Always-on service
pros: Links never die; old decks stay readable.
I am told the moment you submit, whichever chat is open.
cons: A small program always running in the background on this computer.

options.label: Keep it per-chat, restart on demand
pros: No system change.
cons: Links still die; you still have to ask.

options.label: Leave it
pros: Nothing to build.
cons: "Deck died" continues.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: Should a feature have one link, with each round as a tab?
steps.today: Every round of review is a new deck with a new link. One cleanup grew to 108 decks.
steps.problem: You wrote "way too many separate review decks and rounds". Earlier answers are hard to find and each round starts cold.
steps.proposal: One link per feature. Each round is a tab, opening with "since you last looked": what I fixed from your comments and what is new.

options.label: One link, rounds as tabs
pros: Everything about a feature in one place.
Each round starts by showing what changed.
cons: Needs the always-on service from the previous question.

options.label: Separate links, but each opens with "since last round"
pros: Works without the service.
cons: Still many links to keep track of.

options.label: Leave it
pros: Nothing to build.
cons: Rounds stay scattered.

steps.path: Any deck link I send you
steps.headline: What else about the decks still bothers you that I did not ask about?
steps.today: This deck covers answering, context, the final deck and reliability.
steps.problem: I only know the complaints you typed in chat or in a note.
steps.proposal: Anything you write here is added to the redesign. Looks, wording, speed, anything.
steps.prompt: Type anything, or leave it empty…
